name: Proposall
summary: Shopify app for building custom quotes from your products with your own prices and emailing them to customers, with e-signatures on paid plans.
best_for: Shopify stores that send custom quotes on bulk orders and want to build them from their products in a couple of minutes
skip_if: you need signed quotes proven before you pay, or Shopify draft orders already cover your custom orders
honest_knock: We could test only the free plan. The send dialog promises a link to view and sign, but signing is a paid feature, and paid plans could not be selected on a development store, so e-signatures, expiry dates and draft orders stayed untested. The app launched in March 2026 and had no reviews on the Shopify listing when we read it. It asks for customer data, including names, emails and addresses, at install.

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 22 November 2026 on a Shopify development store, with the interface in English. We installed Proposall on its free plan, built a proposal for 12 snowboards at a custom price and sent it by email to a test address. Paid plans could not be chosen on a development store, so we tested none.
findings: Install: right after install the free Launch Pad plan showed 0 of 5 proposals used this month, with no payment screen.
Proposal: we picked a customer, one product, a quantity of 12 and a custom price of $699 instead of $785.95. The total came to $8,388.00, which is 12 x $699, and it took about 2 minutes.
Free limits: e-signatures, expiry dates, a custom layout, a personal message when sending, view analytics, draft orders and proposal history all showed 'Upgrade required' on the free plan.

Sending: the send dialog said it would email a link to view and sign the proposal. The proposal went from draft to sent and the counter showed 1 of 5. Signing is a paid feature, so on the free plan the customer can only view.

Plans: Orbit at $14.99 a month ($149.90 a year) with a 14 day trial adds e-signatures; Mission Control at $39.99 a month ($399.90 a year) adds draft orders from proposals. Both showed 'Unavailable on dev stores' when we tried to select them.
